'''Pell''': {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}}
'''Schneider''': {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Claiborne Pell]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Claiborne Pell]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) | image2 = Schneiderclaudine.jpg }} {{ElectionsRI}} The '''1990 United States Senate election in Rhode Island''' was held on November 6, 1990, to select the [[United States Senate|U.S. senator]] from the state of [[Rhode Island]]. Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] Senator [[Claiborne Pell]] won a sixth and final term, defeating Republican challenger Representative [[Claudine Schneider]] of [[Rhode Island's 2nd congressional district]]. Both candidates were popular in the state, winning their respective primaries unopposed. A large issue in the race was Pell's age, especially following a poor debate performance. Schneider refused to run a negative campaign and avoided attacking Pell, instead emphasizing her opposition to taxes and her "[[tough on crime]]" stance. Rhode Island was seen as one of the most important [[Battleground State|battlegrounds]] in the [[1990 United States Senate elections|1990 Senate cycle]]. The election had a turnout rate of over 40%. Despite being considered among the most vulnerable Democrats, Pell won in a landslide with over 61% of the vote and winning all of the state's counties. However, his margin of victory decreased from 1984. == Background == {{Main|1984 United States Senate election in Rhode Island}} Pell was first elected to the Senate in [[1960 United States Senate election in Rhode Island|1960]]. In 1984, despite [[Ronald Reagan]]'s [[1984 United States presidential election|landslide victory]] in the [[1984 United States presidential election in Rhode Island|concurrent presidential election]],{{Cite news |last=Raines |first=Howell |date=November 7, 1984 |title=Reagan Wins By a Landslide, Sweeping at Least 48 States; G.O.P. Gains Strength in House |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/reagan-wins-by-a-landslide-sweeping-at-least-48-states-gop-gains.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825144938/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/07REAG.html?pagewanted=1 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Pell won a fifth term in the Senate, defeating Republican challenger [[Barbara Leonard (politician)|Barbara Leonard]] with over 70 percent of the vote.{{Cite news |date=November 9, 1984 |title=U.S. Senate |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1146824610/ |access-date=January 23, 2026 |work=[[USA Today]] |page=4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} The 1990 election was held as part of the [[United States midterm election|midterm election cycle]] of Republican President [[George H. W. Bush]]'s term.{{Cite news |last1=Dewar |first1=Helen |last2=Yang |first2=John E. |date=November 6, 1990 |title=The Senate Incumbents Win Control Remains with Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1990/11/07/the-senate/88a317b4-abae-4a7c-9a3c-f65fe6b52b54/ |access-date=March 12, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} Historically, the president's party struggles during the midterms.{{Cite news |last=Hartman |first=Travis |date=November 7, 2022 |title=How does the president's party fare in the midterms? |url=https://www.reuters.com/graphics/USA-ELECTION/MIDTERMS/gdpzyzowgvw/ |access-date=January 24, 2026 |work=[[Reuters]] |language=en}} Prior to the election, Pell's Senate seat was seen as a possible [[Swing state|battleground]].{{Cite news |last=Oreskes |first=Michael |author-link=Michael Oreskes |date=May 6, 1990 |title=GOP undergoes recruiting effort to boost chances |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1091511083/ |access-date=January 24, 2026 |work=[[The Sunday Oregonian]] |page=B7 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[The New York Times]]}} == Candidates and primaries == * [[Claiborne Pell]] (Democrat), incumbent U.S. Senator (1961–1997) * [[Claudine Schneider]] (Republican), U.S. Representative (1981–1991){{Cite web |last=Schneider |first=Claudine |title=Claudine Schneider |url=https://www.congress.gov/member/claudine-schneider/S000136 |access-date=February 24, 2026 |website=[[Congress.gov]]}} Pell had represented Rhode Island in the Senate since 1961 and was seen as one of the most vulnerable Democrats. Schneider had represented [[Rhode Island's 2nd congressional district]] in the [[United States House of Representatives]] since 1981. As her popularity was on par with Pell's, she was seen as the Republican's best chance to flip the seat. The primary elections were held on September 11,{{Cite web |title=Democratic Primary |url=https://elections.ri.gov/elections/results/1990/demprimary.php |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=Rhode Island Board of Elections}} both of them won their respective party's nomination without opposition.{{Cite news |last=Pertman |first=Adam |date=September 16, 1990 |title=GOP, Democrats trade fire across N.E. |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/439414082/ |access-date=January 24, 2026 |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |pages=73–74 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} == General election == In 1989, in the lead up to the election, Pell stated he would attempt to keep his campaign spending to a minimum. While Schneider had set a fundraising goal of $3 million, Pell did not set a goal, but expected to raise around $700,000.{{Cite news |last=Eagleton |first=Tom |date=July 9, 1989 |title=Claiborne Pell will run for re-election without money |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1019995367/ |access-date=January 23, 2026 |work=[[Columbia Daily Tribune]] |page=36 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} === Campaign === An assessment by the [[New York Times News Service|''New York Times'' News Service]] found that both candidates had similar policy positions on most issues. They also noted that Schneider avoided running [[attack ads]] on Pell due to his popularity, instead opting to emphasize her youth and being "[[tough on crime]]". Additionally, her campaign noted that due to Pell's popularity, attack ads would likely backfire.{{Cite news |date=October 12, 1990 |title=Rhode Island Senate race pits youth vs. experience |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/424886963/ |access-date=February 24, 2026 |work=[[The Manhattan Mercury]] |page=C1 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[The Washington Post]]}} However, Pell ran misleading ads which incorrectly stated Schneider was running a negative campaign.{{Cite news |last=Apple Jr. |first=R. W. |date=October 7, 1990 |title=Iraqi invasion puts Pell campaign on more solid ground |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1091766995/ |access-date=January 26, 2026 |work=[[The Sunday Oregonian]] |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[The New York Times]]}} Schneider made her opposition to taxes a key part of her campaign, citing Bush's promise, "[[Read my lips: no new taxes]]", from the [[1988 United States presidential election]]. However, this hurt her after Bush backtracked and raised taxes.{{Cite news |last=Rothberg |first=Donald M. |date=November 10, 1990 |title=This time Bush says he really means it |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1158735372/ |access-date=February 24, 2026 |work=The North Platte Telegraph |page=4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Initially, Pell was expected to lose. At age 71, he was seen as old and out of touch, compared to the relatively young Schneider, age 43.{{Cite news |last=Germond |first=Jack |author-link=Jack Germond |last2=Witcover |first2=Jules |author-link2=Jules Witcover |date=October 16, 1990 |title=Campaign is civil in Rhode Island |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/831330076/ |access-date=February 24, 2026 |work=[[Sun Journal (Lewiston, Maine)|Sun Journal]] |page=4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[The Baltimore Sun]]}} Schneider cited [[John F. Kennedy]]'s line about the nation's need for a "new generation of leaders". The pair debated on August 1. During the debate, Pell was asked what Rhode Island-related bills he had sponsored and sparked backlash after stating that he could not recall any.{{Cite news |last=Phillips |first=Leslie |date=August 24, 1990 |title=R.I.: A leader takes on a legend |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1143021341/ |access-date=January 26, 2026 |work=[[USA Today]] |page=3A |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Afterwards, Pell told a reporter he did not believe his answer should be concerning, attributing it to his poor memory, though he admitted he was primarily focused on committee work and not legislation. During the debate, Schneider continued with her pledge to not negatively campaign, stating "We all love Claiborne Pell." Despite the backlash, Pell, then–chair of the [[United States Senate Committee on Foreign Relations]], saw his popularity increase dramatically following the [[Iraqi invasion of Kuwait]]. Many Republican donors told ''[[The Boston Globe]]'' that if the conflict in the [[Middle East]] continued, Republicans would have a much harder time flipping the seat. However, Robert Rendine, Schneider's campaign manager, noted that despite this, Pell rarely made television appearances, especially compared to other Democrats on the Foreign Relations Committee.{{Cite news |last=Mashek |first=John W. |date=August 20, 1990 |title=Will Bush's stand be popular over time? |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/105991156/ |access-date=February 10, 2026 |work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |page=A-8 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[The Boston Globe]]}} In early November, Pell was seen as likely to hold the seat, though an [[upset victory]] was still believed to be possible.{{Cite news |date=November 6, 1990 |title=No danger |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1105444491/ |access-date=February 17, 2026 |work=[[Gloucester County Times]] |page=D-2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}{{Cite news |last=Farmer |first=John J. |date=November 1, 1990 |title=Women candidates in starring roles |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1150703296/ |access-date=February 17, 2026 |work=[[The Kalamazoo Gazette]] |page=A14 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} === Endorsements === A major topic in the 1990 election cycle was the [[Environmental politics|environment]]. Nationwide, Democrats were seen as more reliable on the issue. Additionally, Pell and Schneider were both [[environmentalists]]. Despite this, Schneider received the endorsement of the environmentalism advocacy organization [[League of Conservation Voters]]. According to Ali Webb, a spokeswoman for the group, stated Schneider was chosen because she prioritized the issue more than Pell did.{{Cite news |last=Foster |first=David |date=August 1, 1990 |title=Conservationists see 'Green Scam' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/366362404/ |access-date=February 10, 2026 |work=[[The Herald-Palladium]] |page=11 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} In August, President Bush and 1984 Democratic vice presidential nominee [[Geraldine Ferraro]] both held [[Stump speech|stump speeches]] throughout [[Providence, Rhode Island]], alongside Schneider and Pell respectively. Schneider criticized Ferraro for supporting Pell, saying, "some people have decided it's politically expedient to be a Democrat first and a woman second."{{Cite news |last=Phillips |first=Leslie |date=August 24, 1990 |title=Ferraro keeps hand in politics |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1143021341/ |access-date=January 26, 2026 |work=[[USA Today]] |page=3A |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} === Results === The election was held on November 6, 1990.{{Cite news |last=Espo |first=David |date=November 7, 1990 |title=Demos win Texas, Florida, four other Governships; Helms wins |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/344952161/ |access-date=January 23, 2026 |work=[[The Times and Democrat]] |pages=A1, A4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Pell, like most incumbents in the [[1990 United States Senate elections]], was reelected to another term. Donald M. Rothberg of the [[Associated Press]] partially attributed Schneider's loss to a lack of public confidence in Republicans after Bush broke his "no new taxes" promise. Pell won in a landslide, receiving just over 60 percent of the vote with a 23 percent margin. He was one of several Democrats to do so despite being seen as vulnerable.{{Cite news |last=Wolf |first=Richard |date=November 8, 1990 |title=With twists, Senate keeps its status quo |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1146858592/ |access-date=February 24, 2026 |work=[[USA Today]] |page=4B |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Despite the large margin, this was a sharp decline from his 45 percent margin of victory in 1984.{{Cite web |date=May 30, 2017 |title=1984 Senatorial General Election Results – Rhode Island |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=44&year=1984&f=0&off=3&class=2 |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}} A total of 10 votes were cast for write-in candidates. The election had a turnout rate of over 40% of registered voters casting ballots, a similar level to the concurrent [[1990 Rhode Island gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]].{{Cite web |last=Liep |first=Dave |title=1990 Senatorial General Election Results – Rhode Island |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=44&year=1990&f=0&off=3&class=2 |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}}{{Cite web |last=Liep |first=Dave |title=1990 Gubernatorial General Election Results – Rhode Island |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=1990&fips=44&off=5&elect=0 |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}} Pell won all five of Rhode Island's counties. His best performance was in [[Providence County, Rhode Island|Providence County]], where he received 65.6 percent of the vote. Schneider's best performance was in [[Kent County, Rhode Island|Kent County]], where she received 44.3 percent of the vote. Additionally, Schneider lost her hometown, [[Narragansett, Rhode Island|Narragansett]].{{Cite news |date=November 7, 1990 |title=GOP hit hard at polls |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/834207724/ |access-date=February 6, 2026 |work=[[Daily Hampshire Gazette]] |page=16 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Despite his large victory, Pell underperformed fellow Democrat [[Bruce Sundlun]]'s margin in the concurrent gubernatorial election by 13 points.{{Election box begin no change | title = 1990 United States Senate election in Rhode Island{{cite web |last=Dendy |first=Dallas L. |title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 6, 1990 |url=http://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1990election.pdf |access-date=January 23, 2026 |website=[[Clerk of the with party link no swing | winner = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{Election box end}} == Aftermath == On January 3, 1991, Pell was sworn in to the [[102nd United States Congress]] by then–Vice President [[Dan Quayle]] alongside his fellow Senators-elect.{{Cite web |date=January 3, 1991 |title=Swearing-In of Senate Members |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/senate-highlight/swearing-in-of-senate-members/10810 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250426220605/https://www.c-span.org/program/senate-highlight/swearing-in-of-senate-members/10810 |archive-date=April 26, 2025 |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=[[C-SPAN]] |language=en-US}} In a 1992 [[Opinion piece]], Republican Senate leader [[Bob Dole]] criticized the lack of media coverage that Schneider, along with other female Republican candidates, received in 1990.{{Cite news |last=Dole |first=Bob |author-link=Bob Dole |date=June 9, 1992 |title=GOP's Women Candidates Get No Respect or Publicity |newspaper=[[Albuquerque Journal]] |department=Opinion |page=7 |agency=''[[The Washington Post]]''}} In 1995, Pell announced he would not seek another term,{{Cite web |date=September 5, 1995 |title=Sen. Pell announces his retirement |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1995/09/05/sen-pell-announces-his-retirement/ |access-date=January 24, 2026 |website=[[The Chicago Tribune]] |language=en-US}} and was succeeded by [[Jack Reed (Rhode Island politician)|Jack Reed]] following the [[1996 United States Senate election in Rhode Island|1996 Senate election]].{{Cite news |date=December 10, 1996 |title=Campaign staff, friends honor Claiborne Pell |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/664795138/ |work=[[The Bangor Daily News]] |page=B6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} == References == {{reflist}} {{United States elections, 1990}} [[Category:1990 elections in Rhode Island]] [[Category:1990 United States Senate elections|Rhode Island]] [[Category:United States Senate elections in Rhode Island|1990]]
